title: DROP TABLE
description: Learn how to drop one or more tables from a database using the DROP TABLE statement.

data.text: The DROP TABLE statement removes one or more tables from a database. When a table is dropped, all its data, triggers, constraints, and permissions are also deleted.

data.title: DROP TABLE Syntax
data.content: Drops a table, optionally using IF EXISTS.

items: Specify the table name to be removed, optionally with schema and database prefixes.
The IF EXISTS clause (SQL Server 2016+) conditionally drops the table only if it exists.
Without IF EXISTS, attempting to drop a non-existent table will result in an error.
You can drop multiple tables in a single statement using a comma-separated list.
Dependent objects like views and stored procedures are not automatically dropped.

data.title: Drop a Non-Existent Table with IF EXISTS
data.content: Drops the revenues table if it exists without error.

data.title: Drop a Single Table
data.content: Creates and then drops the delivery table.

data.text: Drop a Table with a Foreign Key Constraint
SQL Server does not allow dropping a table that is referenced by a foreign key constraint. You must drop the referencing table or constraint first.

data.content: Attempting to drop supplier_groups fails because it is referenced by suppliers.

data.title: Drop Both Tables in Correct Order
data.content: Drops the suppliers table first, then the supplier_groups table.

data.title: DROP TABLE Key Points
points: Use DROP TABLE to remove tables from a database.
Use IF EXISTS to avoid errors for non-existent tables.
Dropping a table also removes its data, triggers, constraints, and permissions.
Drop referencing tables before referenced tables, or drop foreign key constraints first.
You can drop multiple tables in a single statement.
